newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus stock exchange hits all-time low.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus stock exchange hits all-time low.

text.p: Shares on Cyprus's stock exchange hit an all time low of 78.36 on Tuesday, plunging 1.45 percent in a single day amid investor concern about the unstable political climate on the island, analysts said.
The 41-share Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE) all-share index, set at 100 points, has been registering declines since the begining of the year.
Tuesday's close is the lowest level the market has reached since the official opening of the CSE in March 1996. Declines were recorded in all seven sub indices.
"There is a gloomy perception among the public at large about the prospects of the economy," said Haris Christoforou, an economist and Finance Editor of the English-language Cyprus Mail daily.
"People do not want to invest their money in equity, in immovable assets or even borrow money out of the bank," he said.

Christoforou said the gloomy outlook was prompted in part by the unstable political climate and fears it could have a repercussion on tourism, which represents 21 percent of the island's gross domestic product.
"Whether or not it is justified there is a phobia so people prefer to keep the money in their pocket," he told Reuters.
Stavros Agrotis from CISCO stockbrokers agreed that the political climate had affected investor's sentiment. "The market is fundamentally affected by the political situation," he said.
He said one reason for Tuesday's sharp decline was because of need for extra cash to cover Monday's heavy buying. "Some people bought yesterday and sold today," he said.

The CSE index has been declining for several weeks. The decline gained momentum earlier in the month when tension peaked between Cyprus and Turkey over the island's plans to deploy anti-aircraft missiles and Turkish threats they would destroy them.
Banking stocks lost 1.27 percent of their value to close at 88.37. Insurance companies fell 1.42 percent to 56.10.
Trading companies fell 2.33 percent to close at 55.33. Industrial companies closed at 76.97, losing two percent of their value.
